newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Foreign companies consider cement plant in Israel.
newsitem.headline: Foreign companies consider cement plant in Israel.

text.p: Two companies from Japan and Germany are considering a joint venture project with Israel's Pama Energy Resources Development Ltd to build a $300 million cement plant in Israel's Negev desert, a Pama official said on Tuesday.
Japan's Marubeni and Germany's Rohrbach Zement are conducting a feasilibity study for producing cement using oil shale, Pama's managing director Dan Givoni told Reuters.
Givoni said he expected the study would be completed and a decision taken whether to proceed by next summer.
"Part of the feasibility study deals with the size of the plant," he said. "According to a preliminary study the plant should produce about 1.5 million tonnes of cement annually."

Another Pama official said foreign participation was contingent on winning government investment subsidies. The Industry and Trade Ministry said on Tuesday that Marubeni and Pama had met with officials about aid prospects, but it said no official request had been submitted.
The cement plant would be located in Mishor Rotem -- in Israel's southern Negev desert -- where Pama holds the rights to exploit an estimated 1.4 billion tonnes of oil shale.
If the joint venture gets underway, it will be the first domestic producer to compete with Nesher Cement, a joint venture between Koor Industries Ltd and Clal Israel .

Givoni said the unusual production process used oil shale as clinker, a component of cement, and as an energy source. "Because of the unique advantages of oil shale, its (production) cost is competitive, according to our calculations," he added.
Pama is controlled by Israel Electric Corp, Oil Refineries Ltd and Israel Chemicals Ltd.
